root_cause.text: The condition for checking whether the frequency change trigger register is present was inverted, causing the trigger to be skipped when the register is actually present, leading to missing frequency updates during cpufreq scaling.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (common->reg_fc)` to `if (!common->reg_fc)`, indicating the original code incorrectly returned early (skipping the trigger) when `reg_fc` was non-NULL, whereas it should skip only when `reg_fc` is NULL.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix inverted condition to correctly guard against missing frequency change register.
intent_record.what: Inverted the condition from `if (common->reg_fc)` to `if (!common->reg_fc)` in the `ccu_mix_trigger_fc` function.
intent_record.how: The function now returns early when `common->reg_fc` is zero (falsy), rather than when it is non-zero. This changes the control flow: previously it skipped the `ccu_update` call when `reg_fc` existed; now it skips when `reg_fc` is absent.

grouping_result.intent: Fix inverted condition to correctly guard against missing frequency change register.

candidates.rationale: The condition is inverted; it should check for the absence of the register (i.e., if (!common->reg_fc)) to return early only when the register is missing. As written, it returns early when the register is present, skipping the frequency change trigger.
This early return is executed due to the inverted condition, causing the frequency update to be skipped when the register is actually present.

vuln_statements.explanation: The condition is inverted: it should check for the absence of the frequency change trigger register (i.e., !common->reg_fc). As written, when the register is present, the condition is true, causing an early return and skipping the frequency update during cpufreq scaling.
This early return is executed due to the inverted condition, causing the frequency change trigger to be skipped entirely when the register is actually present, leading to missing frequency updates.
